properties.name: Every edge type declares what it means — its primitive relation, sign, possibility and which of its properties are modifiers — and code that needs an edge's meaning can read that declaration instead of keeping its own list
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-09-28, in a dev_reflow2 session: "promote it to intent. then let's implement your suggestion in reflow2" — promoting option (a) of dec:idea-the-schema-declares-what-each-relation-means-in-primitive-terms after asking which finding of the three-graph primitives analysis mattered most for reflow2. Options (b)–(e) of that idea stay ideas.
properties.statement: Every edge type in reflow2's schema carries a declared READING: the primitive relation it is one instance of (part-of, causes, about, norm, source-of …) or the composition of primitives it stands for; its sign and its possibility where it has them; whether its declared direction runs against the primitive's canonical one; which of its own properties are modifiers, and of what kind; and who says so — a model's classification until the owner has reviewed it. The reading is served wherever the vocabulary is served (describe_schema). A check fails when an edge type has no reading, names a primitive or modifier kind outside the declared set, or calls something a modifier that the edge does not declare. And a computation that needs to know what an edge MEANS for its purpose can select edges by reading, rather than by a private list of names that nothing keeps in agreement with the others.
